summary: A key, or a keyboard shortcut, drawn as keycaps in the reader's platform's own symbols and read aloud by name.
useWhen: telling people a shortcut exists — beside a button, in a tooltip, in a command palette row
instructions that name a key: "press Esc to cancel"

useInstead.when: the text is code, a file name or a value
useInstead.why: Kbd means keys to press; `<code>` is the element for code

guarantees: a combination is a <kbd> of <kbd>s, the HTML spec's shape for keys pressed together
the drawn symbols are hidden and a visually hidden copy spells the keys out — "Command K", "Control Shift P" — because ⌘ and ⇧ are read as symbol names or not at all
`mod` resolves to ⌘ on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere; server rendering shows Ctrl and corrects after hydration without a mismatch
requires: the shortcut to be bound somewhere — Kbd shows a key, it does not listen for one

antiPatterns.dont: writing `ctrl+k` or `cmd+k` for the platform's command key
antiPatterns.why: `ctrl` shows a Mac user a key they do not press for it; `cmd` shows everyone else a key they do not have
hand-typed symbols are wrong on the other platform and are read aloud as symbol names
it overrides detection, so half the readers see the other platform's keys; it exists for docs that compare the two
